The paper's Table 4 (an IMAGE, invisible to every text route -- fetched as .t004 PNG and read directly) prints all 15 statements verbatim in the same order as the .sav labels together with each item's % correct. (3) THE ONE MISMATCH IS A TYPO IN THE PAPER, NOT IN THE MAPPING. Table 4 prints 72.77% for Lit6 ("By consuming genetically modified fruit we alter our genes") where the data gives 72.27%. Over n=577 a percentage must be an integer count / 577: 577 x 0.7277 = 419.88, not attainable, while 577 x 0.7227 = 417 exactly. The paper's own Table 4 column also sums to a total-score mean of 12.2683 against the 12.30 its text reports, and the live data gives 12.2634 -- so the table, not the text, is what the data reproduces. (4) OPTION TEXT IS THE SCORED RECODE, NOT THE ADMINISTERED CHOICE. The paper states respondents marked each statement "true", "untrue" or "don't know", and that "[b]oth incorrect and 'don't know' answers were merged into one category, while correct answers comprised the other category making this variable dichotomous". The deposit keeps only the dichotomised variable, so resp 0/1 and the shipped option_text ("Not correct or don't know" / "Correct") are the study's scoring of the response, not the three options respondents saw. The three administered options are not recoverable per item from the deposit and were NOT invented. (5) ENGLISH SHIPPED FOR A CROATIAN ADMINISTRATION. Sample is 577 college- and university-educated people in Croatia; the paper states "All the instruments were translated into Croatian, and then back-translated". Neither the .sav (all labels English; the only Croatian string in the file is the derived variable name Spol_pismenost_interakcija) nor the paper's other supplement (S1 Highlights .docx, five bullets, no instrument) carries any Croatian wording. Documented fallback: English in the base fields, no _translated columns, language=Croatian, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (6) NO INSTRUCTIONS PUBLISHED. Neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces an instruction stem; instructions and section_prompt are NA rather than paraphrased from the Methods sentence. Single trivial section_id. correct_response is NA: resp already encodes scored correctness (1 = Correct), so there is no separate key, and which statements are true vs false is not published in either source. (7) RIGHTS: no block. The Oxford scale of science literacy (Durant, Evans & Thomas 1989 Nature 340:11-14; Miller 1998 Public Underst Sci 7:203-223) is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. No rights-holder page for the scale is locatable and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause could be found to quote; the items circulate through the US National Science Board's Science and Engineering Indicators and Special Eurobarometer 224/516, both public-sector publications, and they are reproduced in full in this CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article's own Table 4 and in its CC BY deposit's variable labels. Silence is permission (irw#1945 test), so extracted normally. Absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause, so this basis is recorded rather than asserted as exhaustive.

BLOCKED -- no item wording recoverable; NO pecino_2018_justice_climate__items.csv WRITTEN (batch_129, 2026-09-10). STEP 3b MISMATCH, and it is the first thing a reader needs: this table is NOT the interpersonal justice climate scale its name and dictionary Description claim. The source article (Pecino V, Manas-Rodriguez MA, Diaz-Funez PA, Aguilar-Parra JM, Padilla-Gongora D, Lopez-Liria R (2018) PLOS ONE 13(11):e0207458, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0207458, CC BY 4.0) measured Interpersonal Justice Climate with 'the Spanish adaptation of Colquitt's Organizational Justice Scale ... This dimension comprises four items' on a 1-5 scale; in the S1 Dataset those are jus12int..jus15int (variable labels 'Interpersonal 12'..'Interpersonal 15', value labels 1 strongly disagree..5 strongly agreed). The live IRW table instead holds cl1ap, cl2ap, cl3in, cl4ap, cl5in, cl6me on a 1-6 scale -- six columns from a separate 40-item 'cl' block the article never names, cites or describes anywhere. data/pecino_2018_interpersonal_justice.py split the 40 cl columns by response-anchor set, not by construct, and the resulting table was named for the paper's headline construct. WHAT THE TABLE ACTUALLY IS: the FOCUS-93 Organizational Climate Questionnaire (Spanish adaptation; Gonzalez-Roma, Tomas, Ferreres et al.). Identified from the deposit's own structure, not guessed: 40 items, the suffixes ap/in/re/me are apoyo/innovacion/reglas/metas, the .sav variable labels for those 40 columns are exactly Support/Innovation/Rules/Goals, and FOCUS-93 is documented as a 40-item instrument answered 1 = 'Nadie' or 'Nunca' to 6 = 'Todos' or 'Siempre' (Rev Psicol Trab Organ 1995;11(30), copmadrid.org/webcopm/publicaciones/trabajo/1995/vol1/arti1.htm) -- which is precisely the two anchor sets in the .sav: cl1-cl6 carry 'No one/Few/Someone/Quite/Considerable/Everyone' and cl7-cl40 carry 'Never/Hardly ever/A few times/Sometimes/Almost always/Always'. So this table is the six 'how many people' FOCUS-93 items. WHY BLOCKED (a text-availability block, not a rights block): no source reachable from the study publishes wording for cl1..cl6. (1) The article's Instruments section prints one sample item for each of the five instruments it describes and FOCUS-93 is not among them. (2) The article's only supporting information is S1 Dataset (the .sav) -- there is no questionnaire, codebook or appendix file. (3) The .sav's variable labels for cl1..cl6 give only the dimension ('Support','Support','Innovation','Support','Innovation','Goals'), which is not an item referent and is shared by three items; its value labels give only the six anchors. Shipping anchors plus a dimension name is the irw#1770 option-only pattern -- no shipped row would carry the item's question -- and FOCUS-93 items do have stems (e.g. the published sample '?Cuanta gente que ha cometido un error ha tenido una segunda oportunidad?'), so the blank-item_text/stemless shape would also be wrong. (4) The canonical FOCUS-93 item list was searched for and not located in numbered form: the Spanish validation literature prints only 8 unnumbered sample items across the four dimensions, and neither the copmadrid article nor the Valencia repository record (roderic.uv.es, HTTP 403 behind Anubis) nor the ResearchGate copy of Van Muijen et al.'s FOCUS questionnaire (HTTP 403) yields items 1-40 with per-item dimension tags. Without that list there is nothing to tie cl1..cl6 to. NO RIGHTS ISSUE WAS REACHED: no clause was located for FOCUS-93 and none is asserted; the block is availability, not rights, and instrument_rights_register.csv has no FOCUS row (do not read this as a ship verdict either -- the question was never reached). WHAT IS VERIFIED AND PARKED: the resp axis is fully settled and the 36 option rows are parked at itemtext/fixes/pecino_2018_justice_climate__items.PARKED.csv with a README. All 36 item x level cell counts in the live table reproduce the .sav's cell counts exactly (cl1ap 4/11/54/79/116/178, cl2ap 8/34/88/114/105/93, cl3in 3/49/142/125/91/32, cl4ap 8/72/134/93/78/57, cl5in 5/27/128/142/93/47, cl6me 3/29/91/101/130/88; n=442 each), so the live integers are the .sav's value-label codes in the labelled direction. Item codes ARE the source column names (the script melts [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('cl')]), so if wording is ever found the mapping needs no positional inference. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE is Spanish (public university, Almeria); every label in the .sav is English, so any future extraction of the anchors alone would be the translated_substitute fallback. (a) The response anchors ship in English: the article gives only the IFSQ's English anchor sets (beliefs disagree/slightly disagree/neutral/slightly agree/agree; behaviours never/seldom/half of the time/most of the time/always) and neither it nor its two supplements publishes the Portuguese equivalents, so option_text is English with option_text_translated empty while item_text is the administered Portuguese.
